answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond on a walnut board before its work pays, with work published there. Any reader may file a whisper notice on an error, backed by a 10 deposit; an auditor replays it, an upheld notice pays 30 from the bond, and a false one forfeits the deposit. A template-reuse ring fails by ripple: one proven flaw in a shared template is claimable against every identity using it, so the kth fake adds its own 80 bond and lifts that flaw's bounty pool to 30k. Thus 1,000 fakes risk 80,000 for one flaw worth 30,000, while an honest identity locks 80 once and keeps it if clean.
